rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for tricking or deceiving someone for your own benefit.

example.english: I made up a fake story to con him out of his money.
example.traditional: 我作咗個假故事，呃走咗佢啲錢。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zok3 zo2 go3 gaa2 gu3 si6 ngaak1 zau2 zo2 keoi5 di1 cin4

rows.note: Use this for a deliberate scam or fraud, especially when money or property is obtained dishonestly.

example.english: The police said the company ran a con to defraud customers.
example.traditional: 警方話嗰間公司用陰招詐騙客戶。
example.jyutping: ging2 fong1 waa6 go2 gaan1 gung1 si1 jung6 jam1 ziu1 zaa3 pin3 haak3 wu6

rows.note: Use this colloquial expression when the emphasis is on taking advantage of someone or making them look foolish.

example.english: Don't think I'm stupid and try to con me.
example.traditional: 你唔好當我冇知，想搵我笨呀？
example.jyutping: nei5 m4 hou2 dong3 ngo5 mou2 zi1 soeng2 wan2 ngo5 ban6 aa3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice for a disadvantage, including in discussions of pros and cons.

example.english: The biggest con of this phone is that its battery runs out quickly.
example.traditional: 呢部手機最大嘅壞處係電量好快用晒。
example.jyutping: ni1 bou6 sau2 gei1 zeoi3 daai6 ge3 waai6 cyu3 hai6 din6 loeng4 hou2 faai3 jung6 saai3

rows.note: Use this for a scam or deceptive scheme carried out to obtain money or another personal gain.

example.english: This online con took many people's savings.
example.traditional: 呢個網上騙局呃走咗好多人嘅積蓄。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 mong5 soeng6 pin3 guk6 ak1 zau2 zo2 hou2 do1 jan4 ge3 zik1 cuk1
